adult: This topic asks you to recognise mixed numbers and improper fractions.
A fraction a/b means a of b equal parts; the parts must be equal in size.
For example, 3/8 of 16 is 6.
It builds on Understanding fractions (age 9+) and leads to Adding Fractions (Unlike Denominators).
kid: A fraction is part of a whole.
The bottom number says how many equal parts. The top says how many we take.
For example, 3/8 of 16 is 6.

adult: This topic is about partition circles and rectangles into two and four equal shares and describe them using the words halves, fourths.
The diameter is twice the radius. Circumference = π × diameter, and area = π × radius².
For example, a circle of radius 4 has area about 50.2.
It builds on Finding halves and quarters (age 5+) and leads to Decomposing a shape into more equal shares.
kid: A circle is round. Every point is the same distance from the middle.
That distance is the radius.
For example, a circle of radius 4 has area about 50.2.
